subject: ZenPeak renewal — anchored rate and commit consolidation proposal
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@zenpeaklabs.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@zenpeaklabs.com>
Date: 2028-01-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal thoughts — rate stability + commit consolidation

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise option that aims to preserve budget predictability for ZenPeak while giving you the extra burst runway you asked for. High level:

- 12 month anchored rate hold (no base price increases for 12 months to give procurement runway)
- Consolidate three existing smaller commits into a single annual commitment to simplify billing and utilization reporting
- One-time bridge credit equal to 10% of expected annual consumption (applied as token-credit against first invoice)
- Optional burst pool: short-term burst capacity (pay-as-you-go beyond committed capacity) with a capped effective rate during surges

I attached a draft term sheet that numbers this out against your Q4 usage baseline. If this looks reasonable, I can loop in finance and legal to draft an order form and route for signatures.

Attachment: ZenPeak_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (PDF)

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm appetite for 12 month anchored rate and the 10% bridge credit.
2) If yes, propose a target date for signature and procurement contacts.

Thanks — available Tue-Wed for a 30 min sync.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@zenpeaklabs.com>

Date: 2028-01-24T14:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal thoughts — rate stability + commit consolidation

Grace,

Appreciate the clear summary. High level we like the direction; two asks from procurement and finance before we can move forward:

1) Anchored rate hold must include a clause that pricing cannot increase for core generation and embedding units for 12 months from signature.
2) We need at least a 20% burst buffer during seasonal traffic (we run a product promo in June) and we'd like an option for converting part of the burst usage into committed units mid-term.

Also, can you send the usage baseline you referenced (monthly token counts) and a simple cost comparison across our current and proposed commitments? Tom from procurement is looped on this thread.

If you can incorporate those things into a counter, we can move quickly.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, ZenPeak Labs
alyssa@zenpeaklabs.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-25T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal thoughts — rate stability + commit consolidation

Team — forwarding ZenPeak's asks. Note: external requests are 1) explicit 12 month no-increase anchor on core units, 2) 20% burst buffer + option to convert burst to commit mid-term, 3) usage baseline and a simple cost comparison.

Can we model the following and come back with a recommended commercial counter and a sanitized term sheet:
- Consolidate 3 commits into single annual commit at a blended rate (propose starting point: current blended rate minus 8% for multi-year simplification)
- Keep an anchored 12 month price hold for core units (generation + embeddings) — what language is acceptable to legal for this?
- Bridge credit suggestion: I proposed 10% in my email; procurement is asking if we can make it 12.5% as concession for the anchored hold and commit consolidation.
- Burst pool: propose a capped surcharge, and provide an option to convert burst into committed units at midpoint with pro-rated credit.

Marcus: could you run through impact on margin for a 12.5% bridge credit + 8% blended discount? Karthik: can you draft a short term-sheet with the conversion clause and a simple example table. Monica: flag any CS support implications if they convert burst mid-term.

Thanks — need this by EOD 2028-02-02 to present a clean counter by next week.

Grace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-02T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal thoughts — rate stability + commit consolidation

Folks — attached is a concise commercial counter and an example P&L impact. Summary of recommended offer to ZenPeak:

- Consolidated annual commit: commit = 1,200M generation tokens + 45M embedding units; blended unit rate = current blended rate less 7.5% (we keep some headroom vs original 8%).
- Anchor: 12 month no-increase clause on those core unit rates (explicitly excludes any new add-on products and professional services).
- Bridge credit: 12.5% of expected first-year spend applied as invoice credit across first 3 invoices.
- Burst pool: up to 20% above committed monthly baseline at a capped surcharge of 1.6x the committed effective rate; conversion option: customer can convert burst usage to committed units once in the 12 month term with a pro-rated application of remaining bridge credit (details in attached term sheet).
- Expected margin impact: ~6.2% reduction in FY28 gross margin on this account under conservative usage; acceptable at scale for retention.

Attachment: ZenPeak_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (updated)
Attachment: ZenPeak_Usage_Baseline_Q4-2027.csv (CSV)

I put in suggested legal language for the anchor (exclusion for price changes driven by GCP/AWS pass-throughs, but not Redwood-initiated base unit repricing within 12 months). If legal pushes back we can tighten to a rate guarantee tied to signed order form.

Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Hi Alyssa and Tom,

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is our formal counter based on the team's recommendations. Key points called out up front:

- 12 month anchored rate for core generation and embedding units (legal language included).
- Consolidated commit and blended rate at minus 7.5% from current blended run-rate.
- Bridge credit: 12.5% of first-year expected spend, applied across first 3 invoices.
- Burst pool up to 20% with capped surcharge; single conversion option to commit mid-term that carries pro-rated treatment of bridge credit.

What we need from ZenPeak to finalize:
1) Confirmation that legal is comfortable with the anchor exclusion for new product SKUs;
2) Confirmation to proceed with the proposed conversion mechanic;
3) Procurement contact for order form routing and preferred signer.

Attachment: ZenPeak_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: ZenPeak_Usage_Baseline_Q4-2027.csv (CSV)

If that all looks good, I'll request finance to build the order form and legal to prepare an amendment. Happy to take a 20 min call to walk through.

Best,
Grace

Grace — thanks. We reviewed with procurement and finance. We can accept the counter with one tweak: the anchor must explicitly state that any pass-through increases tied to third-party infra costs will be limited to a documented cap of 4% annually during the 12 month anchor (procurement insists on predictability). If you can accept that, please route the order form to procurement@zenpeaklabs.com and legal will prepare the SOC2 addendum request (they asked for our standard language).

Assuming you accept the 4% pass-through cap, we are good to sign and will target mid-March for execution.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
